narrative:
Ventral-stream assembly evidence report
======================================

Simple hierarchical MNIST (~64%) applies assembly-calculus project once per layer (LOW->MID->HIGH) with only five Hebbian updates per digit class before cross-class bias. Recurrent cortex (~81%) and the COLT notebook instead run a HIGH->HIGH attractor loop — mathematically multiple project rounds with shared input — which stabilizes IT-like assemblies. Advanced ventral stream (~79%) closes much of the gap by repeated exposure (many project steps per class) and principled readout without recurrence, confirming H1 and H2. Neither path yet encodes parts, completion, or LRI cascade discrimination (H5); those are the plausible assembly-calculus routes toward >95%.

Empirical ladder:
  [0] advanced_recurrent: 80.2% — HIGH->HIGH recurrence matches notebook ~81% regime.
  [0] advanced_ventral: 78.6% — Repeated exposure + connectome readout closes hierarchical gap.
  [0] advanced_fuzzy_lexicon: 78.6% — Language-organ readout on digit IT assemblies.
  [0] baseline_hierarchical: 64.0% — Feedforward 4-area illustration baseline (~64%).
  [A] tier_a_multi_prototype: 62.8% — K-prototype view manifold improves over single prototype.
  [C] tier_c_lri_cascade: 59.0% — LRI competitive cascade on low-margin trials.
  [X] cross_domain_vision_language: 13.2% — Vision and language routes agree via SEMANTIC hub.
  [B] tier_b_consolidation: 10.8% — Systems replay strengthens HIGH->CLASS without reset.
  [A] tier_a_merge_halves: 10.0% — Part-structure merge stream (top/bottom fields).
  [B] tier_b_pattern_complete: 10.0% — Partial cue recovery on HIGH assemblies.
